name: pass-strength-dotted-indicator
title: Password Strength Dotted
description: A password field that fills a row of five dots and ticks off five rules as you type. A status line names the current strength and an eye button reveals what you entered.
use: A sign-up or reset form must show, rule by rule, why a chosen password is accepted or rejected.
avoid: It ships with a fixed 96-width column and five hardcoded rules, so other policies need source edits.
a11y: The input is labelled and described by the strength text, and each rule has a screen-reader suffix; status still leans on colour. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A dark form column on black: a Password label, a rounded input with a placeholder and an eye icon, then five pale rounded bars in a row. Below sits a Must contain line with a strength word and a five-line checklist with tick or cross icons.
behaves: Typing fills the dots from left to right and recolours them green as more rules pass, while each checklist line flips from a cross to a green tick. The eye button switches the field between hidden and visible text.
customise: Takes no props. The five rules, strength words, colours and the fixed column width all live in the source, so another policy or branding needs a file edit.
weight: light: One input, five dots and five checklist rows; no animation loop.
demo: The placeholder Password and, in the last frame, a revealed password reading "stash#2026Ui".
issues: Inactive requirement text is very faint on the black panel.
The fixed 96-width column can overflow a narrow phone.
polishWhy: Clear feedback and tidy spacing; inactive rules are faint and the width never adapts.
